'''Emma Jingfei Zhang''' is a Chinese-American statistician whose research analyzes the statistics of [[complex system]]s including [[Complex network|networks]], [[tensor]]s, and [[point process]]es, and their applications in understanding [[social network]]s, [[Genetic interaction network|gene interactions]], and the [[brain]]. She is Goizueta Foundation Term Associate Professor of Information Systems & Operations Management at [[Emory University]].{{r|dir}}

==Education and career==
Zhang studied mathematics at [[Nankai University]], graduating in 2009. She completed her Ph.D. in statistics in 2014 at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]].{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Statistical Inference on Network Data'', was supervised by [[Yuguo Chen]].{{r|mg}}

She joined the [[University of Miami]] as an assistant professor of [[management science]] in 2014, was promoted to associate professor in 2020, and added a secondary appointment as associate professor of public health sciences in Miami's Miller School of Medicine in 2022. In 2023 she moved to the Department of Information Systems & Operations Management in the [[Goizueta Business School]] of Emory University, with a secondary appointment in the Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics of the [[Rollins School of Public Health]].{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Zhang became an Elected Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 2023.{{r|cv}} In 2025 she was named as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|asa-ims}}
